Ground Water Quality - Van Voast and Hedges (1974) studied the ground-water quality of aquifers in Tract III. Their objectives were to determine the pre-mining hydrologic conditions in the area, and to establish an observation well system around the area of operations of the Westmoreland Resources mine.
Data presented by this study includes: (1) chemical analyses of a number of wells and springs in the area of Westmoreland Resources coal reserves; (2) well data for the Sarpy Creek area near the Westmoreland coal reserves; (3) spring data for the Sarpy Creek area near the Westmoreland Resources coal reserves.
A net work of observation wells was established around the periphery of the proposed mine area in Tract III during the summer of 1973. The wells were drilled to different depths and completed in different aquifers.
Results of this preliminary study indicated that the chemical characteristics of the ground water are diverse, depending on well depth, aquifer, and position in the flow system. Dissolved solids concentrations ranged from 400 to 5,000 mg/l, with a few samples of greater concentration. Laboratory pH values all exceeded 7, with most ranging between 8 and 9. The chemistry of the ground water in the area was not closely related to specific locales or aquifer zones. These workers found water of different types in the Rosebud-McKay zone without any apparent areal pattern. Sodium was noted to be the predominant cation in waters of the Robinson and sub-Robinson zones, and magnesium was found as the predominant cation in waters in the stratigraphically higher zones.
